artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when republishing: the version this publish replaces.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

as.description: The path the file is served at, e.g. index.html or css/site.css. Its extension says what it is served as.

path.description: Give this: the file's absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run.

uri.description: Leave out: the client fills it in.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the tab icon. Pass one when creating.

remove.description: For a republish: served paths to delete, spelled as list_files gives them. A path the artifact does not hold is ignored without an error. To delete and change nothing else, give files as an empty list.

Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. # Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.
- R11 X14 (reference machine) stays OPEN: never name or invent a reference machine, build type or spec anywhere.

## G6 Cross-GDD edits are now allowed
A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

The playtest preset registers only `debug_overlay_mark`; `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only. A tester session can never leave `HIDDEN`. Update DO-2/6/8, AC-DO-170, AC-DO-185.

A wounded victim is not guaranteed an escape (Pillar 3, honest horror). Confirmed; no cooldown or damage floor.

If the target-acquisition spike fails and the lighter fallbacks do not close the gap, `aim_indicator` defaults ON for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Until then D9 (off by default) stands.

I'm checking the consequences of a closed opening isolating a room in vacuum — noting that leaving and sealing the door would leave that room permanently vacated, and realizing the cut hole affects the home side too, since the home ship's keep side is itself the home side.

Then I verify the ragged breach formula for a larger connected volume, confirming the tick count at V_total=120 matches the expected vacuum threshold, and I work through the residual pressure math using the P = n/(V*1000) relationship to check that residuals stay below the 100 dkPa threshold at both V=20 and V=120, consistent with the hysteresis rule for band transitions.

Now I'm checking the staggered graph step timing (every 6 ticks, offset 0–5) against the ±12 tick tolerance for vacuum transition, which holds fine. Then I'm working through the edge case of a save occurring with the avatar inside a vented room — whether a clean generation can be written versus a RISKY one depends on whether the avatar's suit status is CRITICAL at that moment.

Since the suit is non-CRITICAL rather than CRITICAL, I need to verify whether the scripted exit through the door can complete before reserve runs out — this hinges on whether the CRITICAL threshold and drain rate guarantee enough reserve to cross a 20-tile room at walking speed, which I need to check against the Suit's actual parameters rather than assume the fixture just pins it arbitrarily.

Separately, I'm tracing what happens if the player dies in the vented room before the vacuum save writes: they'd restart from the earlier weld-event autosave taken before the cut, which is fine since the cut hasn't happened yet from that save's perspective. But there's a subtler case — if the room reaches vacuum while the suit is still non-CRITICAL, the event save gets released with the breach flag cleared, producing a clean save with the avatar already standing in vacuum.

Then I'm considering suit vitals during extended vacuum exposure: breath reserve depletes until the vitals state crosses CRITICAL, at which point the soft-block kicks in. For a large connected volume, the event save can be withheld for roughly 9.6 minutes, with the regular interval autosave still firing at the 7200-tick mark tagged RISKY in the meantime — a bounded, accepted cost under the earlier ruling, though I'm now second-guessing whether a RISKY save written mid-vent could itself reload into an unwinnable decompression state.

I check rule R15: a QUIT generation without VITALS in its risky_cause is exempt from the fairness step-back, which implies RISKY generations do get stepped over on death restore — so the behavior is consistent. Then I turn to whether a hull breach's virtual hole in a cut compartment stays permanently vented, and whether a later air supply feeding into that compartment could ever restore pressure despite the open hole.

If an O2 supply feeds a vented room with an open hole, the room's equilibrium pressure could actually climb back above the VACUUM threshold, causing the venting flag and ragged_breach_open to flip true again indefinitely — since venting has no ceiling and is only supposed to end once pressure reaches VACUUM. That means saves could be withheld permanently in a scenario where supply rate exceeds the leak rate through the hole, which seems like a genuine edge case worth flagging.

That would require a supply of 5040 mGU/step, which seems large—I need to check the actual vent rate in the Graph data to confirm whether this is plausible, though it seems like a low-probability scenario either way.

The GDD claims the process "ends by construction," so I should flag this as RECOMMENDED: add a ceiling or state a precondition like no O2 source feeding the keep-side room, or inflow below a threshold.

**LS-15 — Seams: a weld moves nothing.** Sections are instantiated into the one world graph when they exist (`instantiate_section`); ids come from the block's `next_*` counters in template order, so a weld **only adds edges** and never renumbers. A weld plan is plain data `{ section_a, section_b, pairs[]: (node_a, port_a, node_b, port_b, loop), openings[]: (comp_a, comp_b, area_max), L_seam, q }` validated by the pure query `can_join(plan)` with the closed reason set `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED` (dormant counts as not loaded), `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `PORT_ABSENT` (ABSENT, DESTROYED or SALVAGED endpoint), `SEAM_LIMIT` (> `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION` 8), `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY` (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 / `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192), `POWER_CYCLE` (the cable pairs would close a cycle in POWER wiring — R12: islands are trees, cycles are rejected here and at data load, VS-A may lift it), `STABILITY` (D.12). It returns the fully resolved plan (slot indices, edge count) and informational `surge[]` per sub-edge (D.14), flagging an opening whose `|ΔP| > WELD_DP_WARN` 300 dkPa — **a warning, never a reject**; the warning is diegetic: the closed hatch's own `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor (CREAK at the rim, rim frost when `|ΔT| > HATCH_DT_FROST_MC`; D.14, LS-14) and the corruptible gauge. `surge[]` reaches the player only through those tells and instruments — never as a number in a weld preview or any other UI; Assembly's preview may consume `surge[].warn` to pick a diegetic cue, not to print the value *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. `weld_join` then only appends the pre-validated edges, writes the SeamRecord, sets every sub-edge **disconnected** (R9: opening `area` 0, pipe and duct valves closed, cable breaker open), bumps `topology_version` and marks `T` + `S/<seam_id>` + `SEC/<a>` + `SEC/<b>`; nothing in it can fail, so CR-9's infallible apply holds. Connecting is then three lit verbs (`set_opening_area`, `set_valve`, `set_breaker`), each with its own surge read-out. The seam weeps through `A_seam_m` from the step it exists (D.2, D.14) until wear-in or a seam PATCH (M7; V11 SEAL_SEAM is the VS-A form) — the weld's own P1 tell. **Structural half, returns, seam read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*: `can_join_static(plan)` is published as a pure query returning the first failing reason of the nine structural reasons in LS-15 order — `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED`, `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `SEAM_LIMIT`, `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY`, `POWER_CYCLE`, `STABILITY` — reading no node `hp`, `state`, `forced_mode` or `served_pm` and computing no `surge[]`; `can_join` adds `PORT_ABSENT` (a node-state read) at its LS-15 position and the `surge[]` read-out. `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`; `seam_view(seam_id)` → `{state, sub_edges[{kind, id}], leak_bp, opening_ids[], cut_sides[]}` is pure *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54 / ASK G10)*: `cut_sides` is empty unless the seam is `CUT` with boundary RAGGED, and then holds one entry per side, `{section_id, cut_holes[{cid, a_hole}], uncapped_open_ends}`, where `cid` is the compartment carrying that side's A_CUT virtual hole (one per former opening), `a_hole` is the hole's CURRENT D.2 area (24 at `hp` 2500; 0 once a Vertical Slice plate install or repair closes it) and `uncapped_open_ends` is the count of that side's fluid ports still `open_end`. It is derived from the hull-stub records and port flags already in `graph.state` (no new persisted field; the SeamRecord tombstone keeps the cut hole ids). The Graph has no keep / leave notion: it returns BOTH sides keyed by `section_id`, and Assembly picks the keep sides from Layout's `keep_sections`. A welded section keeps its `kind` and `rate_pm` (LS-17, LS-25): M2 does not promote a DERELICT section, so a cut restores nothing. An as-welded seam is **not quiet**: it moves nothing between the sections, but it weeps (HISS at the seam) from its first run until wear-in brings `leak_bp` to 0 at period 100 or V1 patches it — the weep tapers **linearly with `leak_bp`** to a cliff at 0 (D.14), not a function of `q`. **Intended seam clock** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a default weld (`q` 850, `L_seam` 3) is tight at period 100 = 16.7 min; the weld-side bay loses about 20 % of its gas over that time if nothing compensates: its total pressure never leaves NORMAL (D.15 SEAM-WEEP), but with its vent isolated its O2 band enters THIN at about step 4,325 (7.2 min) and stays there until the vent runs or the seam is sealed — a deliberate sev-1 tell of the unvented bay, absent with the vent live; V1 PATCH on the seam ends the weep at once (M7 sets `leak_bp` to 0 on a SEAM) and a running vent makes the gas up. The weep carries no LEAK wear (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Alternative considered:* opening the seam at weld with a hard reject above a `ΔP` limit (SD OQ-13) — rejected (R9): it created a vacuum-section soft-lock and a loop-surge leak; the disconnected start removes both and makes every connection a readable choice.
**LS-16 — Cuts, only along seams.** `cut_detach(seam_id, boundary_mode)` is atomic in one P2 apply. `SEALED` (cut at a bulkhead or hatch): the seam's OPENINGs are removed, its loop sub-edges tombstoned, both sides' fluid ports `capped` — nothing leaks. `RAGGED` (cut through the weld): for each former opening a virtual hole of `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment as a hull stub with `hp` 2500 (sev 4 — D.4 gives sev 4 at `hp` ≤ 2500 — BREACH, exogenous — no gate) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G4)*, and each side's fluid ports become `open_end` (SEVERED) leaking at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` (500 ‰ of port cap per step) until `cap_port`. **The two RAGGED hazards are independent** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54)*: `cap_port` (M12) closes a fluid port's hiss only and never changes the hull hole. The A_CUT hull stub (`hp` 2500, `a_hole` 24) has no subject in the MVP: no verb patches, caps or repairs it, so the cut room vents to its steady state, `band_p` VACUUM, and stays a vacuum until a Vertical Slice plate install closes the hole (the same "room is lost" rule as a DESTROYED hull segment). With `n` holes of area A_CUT on a room of volume `V`: `k = G_OPEN × A_CUT × n / (V × GAS_SCALE)`; the room reaches DECOMP (`P` < 400) in `ceil(ln(1000/400)/k)` steps and VACUUM (`P` < 100) in `ceil(ln(1000/100)/k)` steps, `P0` 1000 dkPa nominal. `V` 20, `n` 1: `k` = 2 × 24 / 20000 = 0.0024; DECOMP `ceil(381.8)` = 382 steps = 2,292 ticks (38 s); VACUUM `ceil(959.4)` = 960 steps = 5,760 ticks (96 s). `V` 30, `n` 1: `k` = 0.0016; VACUUM `ceil(1439.1)` = 1,440 steps = 8,640 ticks. A room open to a larger connected volume vents more slowly (`k` uses the connected volume). Guarantees: no inventory lives in edges, so removing them creates or destroys nothing; power has no inventory; the current step's exchange across the seam is simply not computed; one notification batch with `T`, `S/<seam_id>`, affected `C/<id>`; the next run re-derives components. Cutting through a compartment is not a Graph operation and is not allowed (R10): a compartment belongs to one section and a cut never splits gas by a volume ratio. `discard_section(section_id)` (jettison, Web Map unload in VS-A) tombstones a section's slots; mass in it leaves the world and is added to the counters as `discarded_*` so the invariant still closes; ids are never reused.

528	## Formulas
529	
530	Assembly's arithmetic is small on purpose. The Graph owns the seam formulas (`seam_at_weld`, `A_seam_m`, the SEALED/RAGGED hole and open-end rates), Layout the weld offset and detach re-base, Body the docking invariant and `actors_overlapping`, Interaction the channel clock, ledger and subject budget. This section defines only what Assembly owns (`q`, the two offer predicates, host and mate selection, the cut-mode derivation, the pending TTL, the body-count bound, the shape-change time, the CASCADE deadline) and works each cited formula at MVP values so the numbers a reviewer sees are the numbers a test asserts. Every formula is integer arithmetic (the kernel's determinism rule: anything hashed, replicated or replayed is integer or fixed-point); the only fractional values below are display conversions marked as such. Numbering matches the cross-references in Detailed Design (D.2 to D.12 are cited there); D.13 to D.18 are additions. Every formula that Assembly owns is a registry candidate as a **formula** (name, expression, variables), not only as constants (`docs/consistency-failures.md`: register the formula). MVP data: the pair `sock_airlock_e` (home-ship, facing E, `line_px` 720, `start_px` 672) and `sock_b_w` (derelict B, facing W, `line_px` 24, `start_px` 288), `width_tiles` 2, lanes POWER 0 and O2 0, weld offset `(696, 384)` (DA-10), `GRID_24` closure. Where a value is not published by its owner it is marked `[UNV]`.
531	
532	### D.1 Weld quality
533	
534	The weld_quality formula is defined as:
535	
536	`q = clamp( WELD_Q_DEFAULT , Q_MIN , Q_MAX )`, with `Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP / 10))` and `Q_MAX = 990`
537	
538	Derived: `Q_MIN` is the larger of 400 and the smallest `q` whose `hp_seam = q x 10` (`LSG D.14`) is not below `LEAK_HP` (that smallest `q` is `ceil(LEAK_HP / 10)`, so a `LEAK_HP` that is not a multiple of 10 rounds up and the integer-division ambiguity does not arise; the 400 outer floor holds across the Graph's 2000-6000 `LEAK_HP` range); `Q_MAX` is the registered 990, 3 permille under the first `q` (993) at which the Graph's weep is 0 from birth (`LSG D.2`, floor form) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: re-justified; the earlier "10 permille under the q = 1000 cliff" came from the superseded ceiling form. Q_MAX stays 990, a registered value, but a weld at Q_MAX now weeps only 2 milli flow units for about 6.3 minutes, so it is the faintest legal weld, not a still-weeping one)*. The clamp runs once, at data load, never per weld; a clamped value raises the diagnostic `MSA_Q_CLAMPED`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **this is the one place the range of `q` is stated**: `Q_MIN(LEAK_HP)` to 990, which is 400 to 990 at the default `LEAK_HP` 4000 and 600 to 990 at 6000. Every other mention (MSA-13, T9, T17, FB-8, VA-15) cites D.1.)* The rule has no other term: there is no `sum q_mods`, no per-weld input and no state read.
539	
540	**Variables:**
541	
542	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
543	|---|---|---|---|---|
544	| `WELD_Q_DEFAULT` | int (permille) | 400-990, default 850 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | data file (registry candidate ★) | The one weld-quality constant; refines advisor R11 (was 400-1000) |
545	| `LEAK_HP` | int (bp) | 2000-6000, default 4000 | Graph tuning (cited, locked) | Below this a fluid sub-edge starts in LEAK |
546	| `Q_MIN` | int (permille) | 400-600 (400 at `LEAK_HP` <= 4000; 600 at 6000) | derived | Lower clamp; moves with `LEAK_HP`, never below 0 |
547	| `Q_MAX` | int (permille) | 990 | derived (`1000 - 10`) | Upper clamp |
548	| `q` | int (permille) | `Q_MIN`..990 | calculated | The value placed in the plan handed to `weld_join` and stored on the SeamRecord |
549	
550	**Output Range:** 400 to 990 inclusive. Two named cliffs sit just outside it. *Below 400:* `hp_seam` falls under `LEAK_HP` and every fluid sub-edge of the seam starts in LEAK mode, a leak with no prior tell (a P2 fairness break). *At q 993 and above (1000 is the limiting case):* `A_seam_m` is 0 from the first period, the seam has no weep and the weld loses its P1 tell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `A_seam_m` is the Graph's (`LSG D.2`) and falls linearly with `leak_bp`, which wears in by 100 bp per 10 s period from 10000 (`leak_bp = 10000 - 100 x period`); the table is worked at registry defaults for `L_seam` 2 and states no expression. Within the range the Graph's consequences are physical and cited, not restated (below, `L_seam` 2, cable port caps 3000):
551	
552	| `q` | `(500 + q/2)` permille of the lesser port | `cap_seam` (W) | `hp_seam` | `A_seam_m` at period 0 (milli flow units, `L_seam` 2) | `A_seam_m` at period 50 | weep ends | verdict |
553	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
554	| 399 (loaded as-is, would clamp to 400) | 699 | 2097 | 3990 (below `LEAK_HP` 4000) | 11,558 | 5,778 | period 100 | leaks at birth: outside the range |
555	| 400 | 700 | 2100 | 4000 (not below) | 11,520 | 5,760 | period 100 | the lower bound |
556	| 700 | 850 | 2550 | 7000 (`HP_OK` boundary) | 2,880 | 1,440 | period 100 | legal, tight |
557	| 850 | 925 | 2775 | 8500 | 720 | 360 | period 100 (about 16.7 min) | the MVP default |
558	| 990 | 995 | 2985 | 9900 | 2 | 0 | period 38 (about 6.3 min) | the upper bound: a faint, short weep |
559	| 1000 (loaded as-is, would clamp to 990) | 1000 | 3000 | 10000 | 0 | 0 | none | no weep at birth: outside the range |
560	
561	**Example:** the data file ships `WELD_Q_DEFAULT = 850`: no clamp, `q = 850`, `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` not raised. A modder or a bad edit ships 1000: the loader clamps to 990, raises `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` once at load, the weld produces `A_seam_m` 2 at period 0 (a faint weep that ends at period 38, about 6.3 minutes) and the Graph's descriptor keeps `intensity_pm` at least 1 while it flows (LS-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
562	
563	### D.2 Offer predicates
564	
565	The weld_offer formula is defined as:
566	
567	`weld_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_welder ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == FREE ) AND ( |Pairs(s)| >= 1 )`, with `Pairs(s) = { (a, b) : s IN {a, b} AND host_of(a, b) AND can_attach(a, b) == OK AND docked(a, b, frame_shift_px(a, b)) }` and `host_of` the host rule of D.3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier form defined `weld_offer` through a host socket `a` that D.3 defined through the same candidate set; the focused socket `s` now seeds the candidate pairs and D.3 only chooses among them)*
568	
569	Derived: the prompt `E . Weld` exists iff `weld_offer` is true. The predicate reads no node or edge accessor, calls neither `can_join_static` nor the full `can_join`, and reads no `surge[]` (MSA-9, MSA-12). The carry lockout (a seat carrying an item gets no channelled verb, PC-7, IA-28) is Interaction's selector, not a term here; a carrying seat therefore never sees the weld prompt and `begin_weld` is a `BUSY` backstop.
570	
571	**Variables:**
572	
573	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
574	|---|---|---|---|---|
575	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_welder` is class {1, 9}, slot 2, equipped at start) | The equipped tool |
576	| `lit(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Emitter State via Interaction's lit check | The socket subject is lit (lit-only channelled verbs, PC-7) |
577	| `in_reach(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Interaction reach geometry, `REACH_PX` 72 | The socket subject is within reach |
578	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | `FREE`, `WELDED`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` | Layout (LY-13) | Terminal lifecycle (S3) |
579	| `can_attach(a, b)` | enum | `OK` or one of eight reasons | Layout (LY-14) | The mating verdict |
580	| `frame_shift_px(a, b)` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid | Layout `LY D.6` (ASK L3 asks for it as a pure read) | The shift the weld would apply (D.5) |
581	| `docked(a, b, fs)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Body `BDY D.8` | The two bodies already sit at the weld offset with equal velocity |
582	| `Pairs(s)` | set of ordered socket pairs `(a, b)` | 0..`MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` x `MAX_SECTIONS` in principle; exactly 0 or 1 in MVP | calculated | The ordered pairs that contain the focused socket `s`, put in host order by D.3, and pass both `can_attach` and `docked` |
583	| `weld_offer` | bool | 0 or 1 | calculated | Whether the prompt exists |
584	
585	**Output Range:** boolean. Pure and total: no side effect, no module-body state. In MVP `|Pairs|` is 0 or 1 by authoring (one socket pair); with several candidate pairs `[VS]` D.3 selects the lowest key pair. Per-call cost is O(1) over cached static data (`MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US`, set in the spike).
586

588	
589	The seam_cut_offer formula is defined as:
590	
591	`seam_cut_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_cutter ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == WELDED ) AND ( seam_state(seam_of(s)) == ACTIVE ) AND ( foot_section(seat) IN keep_sections(seam_of(s)) )`
592	
593	Derived: `keep_sections` is the component of the weld forest that keeps its `body_id` (the one containing the body's `origin_section_id`, LY-17; in MVP the home-ship side), from Layout's `detach_preview` (ASK L1). 594	
595	**Variables:**
596	
597	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
598	|---|---|---|---|---|
599	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_cutter`, class {8}, slot 1) | The equipped tool |
600	| `lit`, `in_reach` | bool | 0 or 1 | as above | |
601	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | as above | Layout | Must be `WELDED` |
602	| `seam_of(s)` | seam id | `seam_id` allocated by the Graph | Layout `welds[]` | The seam the socket is part of |
603	| `seam_state` | enum | `ACTIVE`, `CUT` | Layout / Graph | Only an `ACTIVE` seam can be cut |
604	| `foot_section(seat)` | section id | a section of the seat's body | Body `BDY D.10` | The section containing the seat's foot **origin** (BDY-23) |
605	| `keep_sections(seam)` | set of section ids | 1..`MAX_SECTIONS` | Layout `detach_preview` (ASK L1) | Sections that keep `body_id` after the cut |
606	
607	**Output Range:** boolean. **Example:** welded pair, seat standing in the home-ship airlock (a section in the home component): offer = 1. A `FREE` socket: offer = 0 (state must be `WELDED`); a `CAPPED` socket: offer = 0 (terminal).

612

615	Derived: if both sections are DERELICT `[VS]`, `host_of` instead holds for the ordering whose `socket_a` is on the body with the lower `body_id`. **When the HOME section has several sockets** `[VS]`, a seat focusing a derelict socket `s` has one candidate pair per FREE HOME socket that passes `can_attach` and `docked`, and the pair with the lowest `socket_key_a` wins, then the lowest `socket_key_b`; a seat focusing a HOME socket has `socket_a = s` and the tie-break runs over the mates. 620	|---|---|---|---|---|

622	| `body_id` | int | 0..`MAX_BODIES` - 1 | Layout | The tie-break for a two-derelict pair `[VS]` |

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

528	## Formulas
529	
530	Assembly's arithmetic is small on purpose. The Graph owns the seam formulas (`seam_at_weld`, `A_seam_m`, the SEALED/RAGGED hole and open-end rates), Layout the weld offset and detach re-base, Body the docking invariant and `actors_overlapping`, Interaction the channel clock, ledger and subject budget. This section defines only what Assembly owns (`q`, the two offer predicates, host and mate selection, the cut-mode derivation, the pending TTL, the body-count bound, the shape-change time, the CASCADE deadline) and works each cited formula at MVP values so the numbers a reviewer sees are the numbers a test asserts. Every formula is integer arithmetic (the kernel's determinism rule: anything hashed, replicated or replayed is integer or fixed-point); the only fractional values below are display conversions marked as such. Numbering matches the cross-references in Detailed Design (D.2 to D.12 are cited there); D.13 to D.18 are additions. Every formula that Assembly owns is a registry candidate as a **formula** (name, expression, variables), not only as constants (`docs/consistency-failures.md`: register the formula). MVP data: the pair `sock_airlock_e` (home-ship, facing E, `line_px` 720, `start_px` 672) and `sock_b_w` (derelict B, facing W, `line_px` 24, `start_px` 288), `width_tiles` 2, lanes POWER 0 and O2 0, weld offset `(696, 384)` (DA-10), `GRID_24` closure. Where a value is not published by its owner it is marked `[UNV]`.
531	
532	### D.1 Weld quality
533	
534	The weld_quality formula is defined as:
535	
536	`q = clamp( WELD_Q_DEFAULT , Q_MIN , Q_MAX )`, with `Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP / 10))` and `Q_MAX = 990`
537	
538	Derived: `Q_MIN` is the larger of 400 and the smallest `q` whose `hp_seam = q x 10` (`LSG D.14`) is not below `LEAK_HP` (that smallest `q` is `ceil(LEAK_HP / 10)`, so a `LEAK_HP` that is not a multiple of 10 rounds up and the integer-division ambiguity does not arise; the 400 outer floor holds across the Graph's 2000-6000 `LEAK_HP` range); `Q_MAX` is the registered 990, 3 permille under the first `q` (993) at which the Graph's weep is 0 from birth (`LSG D.2`, floor form) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: re-justified; the earlier "10 permille under the q = 1000 cliff" came from the superseded ceiling form. Q_MAX stays 990, a registered value, but a weld at Q_MAX now weeps only 2 milli flow units for about 6.3 minutes, so it is the faintest legal weld, not a still-weeping one)*. The clamp runs once, at data load, never per weld; a clamped value raises the diagnostic `MSA_Q_CLAMPED`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **this is the one place the range of `q` is stated**: `Q_MIN(LEAK_HP)` to 990, which is 400 to 990 at the default `LEAK_HP` 4000 and 600 to 990 at 6000. Every other mention (MSA-13, T9, T17, FB-8, VA-15) cites D.1.)* The rule has no other term: there is no `sum q_mods`, no per-weld input and no state read.
539	
540	**Variables:**
541	
542	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
543	|---|---|---|---|---|
544	| `WELD_Q_DEFAULT` | int (permille) | 400-990, default 850 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | data file (registry candidate ★) | The one weld-quality constant; refines advisor R11 (was 400-1000) |
545	| `LEAK_HP` | int (bp) | 2000-6000, default 4000 | Graph tuning (cited, locked) | Below this a fluid sub-edge starts in LEAK |
546	| `Q_MIN` | int (permille) | 400-600 (400 at `LEAK_HP` <= 4000; 600 at 6000) | derived | Lower clamp; moves with `LEAK_HP`, never below 0 |
547	| `Q_MAX` | int (permille) | 990 | derived (`1000 - 10`) | Upper clamp |
548	| `q` | int (permille) | `Q_MIN`..990 | calculated | The value placed in the plan handed to `weld_join` and stored on the SeamRecord |
549	
550	**Output Range:** 400 to 990 inclusive. Two named cliffs sit just outside it. *Below 400:* `hp_seam` falls under `LEAK_HP` and every fluid sub-edge of the seam starts in LEAK mode, a leak with no prior tell (a P2 fairness break). *At q 993 and above (1000 is the limiting case):* `A_seam_m` is 0 from the first period, the seam has no weep and the weld loses its P1 tell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `A_seam_m` is the Graph's (`LSG D.2`) and falls linearly with `leak_bp`, which wears in by 100 bp per 10 s period from 10000 (`leak_bp = 10000 - 100 x period`); the table is worked at registry defaults for `L_seam` 2 and states no expression. Within the range the Graph's consequences are physical and cited, not restated (below, `L_seam` 2, cable port caps 3000):
551	
552	| `q` | `(500 + q/2)` permille of the lesser port | `cap_seam` (W) | `hp_seam` | `A_seam_m` at period 0 (milli flow units, `L_seam` 2) | `A_seam_m` at period 50 | weep ends | verdict |
553	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
554	| 399 (loaded as-is, would clamp to 400) | 699 | 2097 | 3990 (below `LEAK_HP` 4000) | 11,558 | 5,778 | period 100 | leaks at birth: outside the range |
555	| 400 | 700 | 2100 | 4000 (not below) | 11,520 | 5,760 | period 100 | the lower bound |
556	| 700 | 850 | 2550 | 7000 (`HP_OK` boundary) | 2,880 | 1,440 | period 100 | legal, tight |
557	| 850 | 925 | 2775 | 8500 | 720 | 360 | period 100 (about 16.7 min) | the MVP default |
558	| 990 | 995 | 2985 | 9900 | 2 | 0 | period 38 (about 6.3 min) | the upper bound: a faint, short weep |
559	| 1000 (loaded as-is, would clamp to 990) | 1000 | 3000 | 10000 | 0 | 0 | none | no weep at birth: outside the range |
560	
561	**Example:** the data file ships `WELD_Q_DEFAULT = 850`: no clamp, `q = 850`, `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` not raised. A modder or a bad edit ships 1000: the loader clamps to 990, raises `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` once at load, the weld produces `A_seam_m` 2 at period 0 (a faint weep that ends at period 38, about 6.3 minutes) and the Graph's descriptor keeps `intensity_pm` at least 1 while it flows (LS-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

563	### D.2 Offer predicates
564	
565	The weld_offer formula is defined as:
566	
567	`weld_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_welder ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == FREE ) AND ( |Pairs(s)| >= 1 )`, with `Pairs(s) = { (a, b) : s IN {a, b} AND host_of(a, b) AND can_attach(a, b) == OK AND docked(a, b, frame_shift_px(a, b)) }` and `host_of` the host rule of D.3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier form defined `weld_offer` through a host socket `a` that D.3 defined through the same candidate set; the focused socket `s` now seeds the candidate pairs and D.3 only chooses among them)*
568	
569	Derived: the prompt `E . Weld` exists iff `weld_offer` is true. The predicate reads no node or edge accessor, calls neither `can_join_static` nor the full `can_join`, and reads no `surge[]` (MSA-9, MSA-12). The carry lockout (a seat carrying an item gets no channelled verb, PC-7, IA-28) is Interaction's selector, not a term here; a carrying seat therefore never sees the weld prompt and `begin_weld` is a `BUSY` backstop.
570	
571	**Variables:**
572	
573	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
574	|---|---|---|---|---|
575	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_welder` is class {1, 9}, slot 2, equipped at start) | The equipped tool |
576	| `lit(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Emitter State via Interaction's lit check | The socket subject is lit (lit-only channelled verbs, PC-7) |
577	| `in_reach(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Interaction reach geometry, `REACH_PX` 72 | The socket subject is within reach |
578	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | `FREE`, `WELDED`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` | Layout (LY-13) | Terminal lifecycle (S3) |
579	| `can_attach(a, b)` | enum | `OK` or one of eight reasons | Layout (LY-14) | The mating verdict |
580	| `frame_shift_px(a, b)` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid | Layout `LY D.6` (ASK L3 asks for it as a pure read) | The shift the weld would apply (D.5) |
581	| `docked(a, b, fs)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Body `BDY D.8` | The two bodies already sit at the weld offset with equal velocity |
582	| `Pairs(s)` | set of ordered socket pairs `(a, b)` | 0..`MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` x `MAX_SECTIONS` in principle; exactly 0 or 1 in MVP | calculated | The ordered pairs that contain the focused socket `s`, put in host order by D.3, and pass both `can_attach` and `docked` |
583	| `weld_offer` | bool | 0 or 1 | calculated | Whether the prompt exists |
584	
585	**Output Range:** boolean. Pure and total: no side effect, no module-body state. In MVP `|Pairs|` is 0 or 1 by authoring (one socket pair); with several candidate pairs `[VS]` D.3 selects the lowest key pair. Per-call cost is O(1) over cached static data (`MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US`, set in the spike).
586	
587	**Example:** the seat holds the welder, stands lit within 72 px of `sock_airlock_e`; the socket is `FREE`; `sock_b_w` passes `can_attach` (facings E and W are opposite, `width_tiles` 2 and 2, `SOCKET_CLASS` 1 and 1, lane multisets equal, no `GEOM_OVERLAP` under Layout's `rects_in` test: the home `spine_corridor` east hull wall is x [672, 696) per Derelict Authoring D.13); B is docked at `frame_shift_px = (696, 384)`: `|Pairs| = 1`, offer = 1, the prompt shows. The same stance with B still 24 px short of its dock (`world(b) - world(a) = (720, 384)`): `docked` is false, `|Pairs| = 0`, offer = 0, **no prompt and no "can't weld" icon**.
588	
589	The seam_cut_offer formula is defined as:
590	
591	`seam_cut_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_cutter ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == WELDED ) AND ( seam_state(seam_of(s)) == ACTIVE ) AND ( foot_section(seat) IN keep_sections(seam_of(s)) )`
592	
593	Derived: `keep_sections` is the component of the weld forest that keeps its `body_id` (the one containing the body's `origin_section_id`, LY-17; in MVP the home-ship side), from Layout's `detach_preview` (ASK L1). There is deliberately **no `CUT_BLOCKED` term**: the prompt is offered, `CUT_BLOCKED` is checked at begin, handoff and completion (D.13), and the clean hatch-presence oracle stays a rejection the player can see (MSA-21).
594	
595	**Variables:**
596	
597	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
598	|---|---|---|---|---|
599	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_cutter`, class {8}, slot 1) | The equipped tool |
600	| `lit`, `in_reach` | bool | 0 or 1 | as above | |
601	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | as above | Layout | Must be `WELDED` |
602	| `seam_of(s)` | seam id | `seam_id` allocated by the Graph | Layout `welds[]` | The seam the socket is part of |
603	| `seam_state` | enum | `ACTIVE`, `CUT` | Layout / Graph | Only an `ACTIVE` seam can be cut |
604	| `foot_section(seat)` | section id | a section of the seat's body | Body `BDY D.10` | The section containing the seat's foot **origin** (BDY-23) |
605	| `keep_sections(seam)` | set of section ids | 1..`MAX_SECTIONS` | Layout `detach_preview` (ASK L1) | Sections that keep `body_id` after the cut |
606	
607	**Output Range:** boolean. **Example:** welded pair, seat standing in the home-ship airlock (a section in the home component): offer = 1. The same seat standing in derelict B's `b_dock`: `foot_section` is in the leaving component, offer = 0 and **no cut prompt exists on the derelict side** (the self-strand trap is unreachable). A `FREE` socket: offer = 0 (state must be `WELDED`); a `CAPPED` socket: offer = 0 (terminal).
608	
609	### D.3 Host and mate selection
610	
611	The host_and_mate formula is defined as:
612	
613	`host_of(a, b) = ( kind(sec(a)) == HOME AND kind(sec(b)) == DERELICT )` ; `(socket_a, socket_b) = argmin over Pairs(s) of ( socket_key_a , socket_key_b )` in that lexicographic order, with `Pairs(s)` as in D.2; the pair is empty when `Pairs(s)` is empty *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the section variable is renamed `sec` so `s` means only a socket; the focused socket seeds `Pairs(s)`; and the tie-break over candidate pairs is stated)*
614	
615	Derived: if both sections are DERELICT `[VS]`, `host_of` instead holds for the ordering whose `socket_a` is on the body with the lower `body_id`. **When the HOME section has several sockets** `[VS]`, a seat focusing a derelict socket `s` has one candidate pair per FREE HOME socket that passes `can_attach` and `docked`, and the pair with the lowest `socket_key_a` wins, then the lowest `socket_key_b`; a seat focusing a HOME socket has `socket_a = s` and the tie-break runs over the mates. In the MVP there is one pair, so no tie-break fires. The seat may stand on either side and focus either socket; Assembly derives the ordered pair, so the surviving body is always the home-ship's and the absorbed derelict body is re-based (LY-16 / LY Open Question 21: confirmed).
616	
617	**Variables:**
618	
619	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
620	|---|---|---|---|---|
621	| `kind(s)` | enum | `HOME`, `DERELICT` | Graph LS-17 | Section kind |
622	| `body_id` | int | 0..`MAX_BODIES` - 1 | Layout | The tie-break for a two-derelict pair `[VS]` |
623	| `socket_key` | string id | stable, ordered by byte comparison | Layout | The tie-break among several candidate pairs `[VS]` |
624	| `sec(x)` | section id | a section of the loaded set | Layout | The section a socket belongs to *(renamed from the reused `s`, re-review)* |
625	| `Pairs(s)` | set | as D.2 | calculated | Candidate ordered pairs containing the focused socket |
626	
627	**Output Range:** one ordered pair `(socket_a, socket_b)` or the empty pair (no offer). Deterministic: the same state always selects the same pair, which replay and MIRROR rely on. **Example:** the seat stands in derelict B's `b_dock` and focuses `sock_b_w`; `kind(derelict_b)` is DERELICT, `kind(home_ship)` is HOME; the pair is `(sock_airlock_e, sock_b_w)` regardless of which socket was focused, and B is the absorbed side.
628	
629	### D.4 Seam properties at weld (cited from the Graph, worked at MVP values)
630	
631	The seam_at_weld formula is defined as:
632	
633	`plan_seam = seam_at_weld( q , cap_a , cap_b , L_seam )`; **owned by the Graph (`LSG D.14`, registry `seam_at_weld`; `LSG D.2` for `A_seam_m`); Assembly supplies `q` (D.1) and the plan's `L_seam`, restates no expression and adds no term**
634	
635	**Variables:**
636	
637	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
638	|---|---|---|---|---|
639	| `q` | int (permille) | `Q_MIN` to 990 (D.1) | D.1 | Supplied by Assembly |
640	| `L_seam` | int (tiles) | 1-12 | Layout `width_tiles`, via `socket_plan` | MVP value 2 |
641	| `cap_a`, `cap_b` | int (loop units per step) | per port | the two joined ports' `cap` (Item DB defs; authored for bare nodes) | POWER lane: `mod_breaker_junction` CABLE ports, 3000 each (Item DB def 12, AC-79). O2 lane: `dj_air` and `dj_b_dock` are bare DUCT_JUNCTION nodes whose `cap` no design file publishes: **GAP, symbol `cap_duct`, `[UNV]`**, ASK G6(d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: still unpublished after three routings with no owner (Item DB Open Question 30, Graph open-question row 26, OQ-DA-33). The only O2-lane value that depends on it is `cap_seam`; `hp_seam`, `leak_bp` and `A_seam_m` do not, and are worked below. Proposed working value for the owner to confirm or replace: `cap_duct` = 1200 mGU/step, equal to the largest O2-lane port in the Item DB (`mod_o2_tank`, retuned cap 1200), so the junction is never the bottleneck of the lane it joins. It is a proposal, not a fact, and no assertion rests on it until the owner publishes the value and the registry carries it as `cap_duct_junction`.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: **owner assigned: Derelict Authoring**, which authors the bare DUCT_JUNCTION nodes `dj_air` and `dj_b_dock` (DA-19). It is asked to publish `cap_duct_junction` in the registry; the proposed 1200 mGU/step is acceptable as the first value `[PLACEHOLDER]`. Severity: the creative-director rules this RECOMMENDED, because implementation starts on the injected value; the owner must be assigned before the O2-weld Integration story starts, and it is (routed as a hard requirement in T13).)* |
642	| `A_SEAM_MAX`, `SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP`, `SEAM_WEARIN_BP_PER_100`, `WELD_DP_WARN`, `LEAK_HP` | int | 16, 10000, 100, 300 dkPa, 4000 | Graph tuning (cited, locked) | Used only inside the Graph's expressions |
643	
644	**Output Range:** the Graph's own: `cap_seam` 700 to 995 permille of the lesser port across Assembly's `q` range, `hp_seam` 4000 to 9900, `leak_bp` starts at 10000, `A_seam_m` per `LSG D.2`.
645	
646	**Example (MVP POWER lane, `q` 850):** `cap_a = cap_b = 3000`; `cap_seam = floor(3000 x 925 / 1000) = 2775 W`; `hp_seam = 8500` (above `HP_OK` 7000 and `LEAK_HP` 4000); `leak_bp = 10000`; `A_seam_m` = 720 milli flow units at period 0 (the Graph's value, LSG D.2: 360 per tile over 2 tiles), 360 at period 50 and 0 at period 100 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The O2 lane: `cap_seam = floor( min(cap_duct_a, cap_duct_b) x 925 / 1000 )`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: completed as far as the data allows. **O2 lane at `q` 850, `L_seam` 2:** `hp_seam` = 8500, `leak_bp` = 10000 and `A_seam_m` = 720 at period 0, all independent of the duct port cap and identical to the POWER lane, because `A_seam_m` depends only on `q`, `L_seam` and `leak_bp` (`LSG D.2`); **verified against LSG D.14 (2026-10-27):** `hp_seam = q x 10`, `leak_bp = SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP` and `A_seam_m` per D.2 are computed per seam from `q`, `L_seam` and `leak_bp`, and only `cap_seam = floor(min(cap_a, cap_b) x (500 + q/2) / 1000)` reads the ports' caps. `cap_seam` is `floor(min(cap_duct_a, cap_duct_b) x 925 / 1000)`: with the proposed `cap_duct` 1200 `[UNV]` it would be `floor(1200 x 925 / 1000)` = 1110 mGU/step; with a hypothetical 800 it would be 740; the AC asserts the formula with the injected value, and asserts the number only once the owner publishes `cap_duct`. The O2 half of the weld Integration story is the only work gated on this: the kernel, the PROJECTOR (S3), the fault model (S6) and the power-lane weld proceed.)* Wear-in (cited): `leak_bp` falls 100 bp per 10 s period from 10000, so the weep tapers linearly (720, 360 and 0 milli at periods 0, 50 and 100 for `q` 850) and stops at period 100: `100 x 10 s = 1000 s`, about 16.7 minutes; at `q` 990 it is 2 milli until `leak_bp` falls below 6250 (period 38, about 6.3 minutes) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Surge (cited, `LSG D.14`): home bay at 1000 dkPa against a derelict room at 150 dkPa gives `|dP|` = 850 > `WELD_DP_WARN` 300, so `surge[].warn` is true and the closed hatch creaks (`SEAL_STRAIN`); the weld is permitted and moves nothing. Assembly's cue reads `warn` as a boolean only (MSA-15).

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.
