648	### D.5 Weld offset prediction and the actor invariant
649	
650	The frame_shift_prediction_equal formula is defined as:
651	
652	`frame_shift_px = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b - offset_b_old` ; the apply asserts `LM2.frame_shift_px == predicted` (else `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`) ; `docked(a, b, fs) = ( vel(a) == vel(b) ) AND ( world(b) - world(a) == fs )` ; `abs(actor) = world(body) + pos_curr`
653	
654	Derived: the first is Layout's `LY D.6` (attach), the third Body's `BDY D.8`; Assembly computes nothing new, it compares the value predicted in `validate` (V3) with the value LM2 returns (A3) and BM3 consumes (A4). Because `offset_a`, `pos_a` and `pos_b` all lie on the 24-px grid (`GRID_24` lint), so does the result (the 24-grid closure, `LY D.6`).
655	
656	**Variables:**
657	
658	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
659	|---|---|---|---|---|
660	| `offset_a`, `offset_b_old` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid; `(0, 0)` for a freshly built single-section body (LY-25) | Layout | Host section offset in the surviving body; absorbed section offset in its own body |
661	| `pos_a`, `pos_b` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid, local >= 0 | Layout socket reference points: `(line_px, start_px)` for facing E or W | The two sockets' reference points |
662	| `frame_shift_px` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid, far below `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` 2^22 | calculated (Layout) | The absorbed body's frame origin in the host frame; every absorbed section GAINS it |
663	| `world(a)`, `world(b)`, `vel(a)`, `vel(b)` | int pairs | Body ranges | `body.state` | Exterior poses and velocities |
664	| `pos_curr` | int pair (px) | in the actor's body frame | `body.state` | The actor's position |
665	
666	**Output Range:** exact integers. `delta_abs = frame_shift_px - (world(b) - world(a))` is `(0, 0)` iff the position half of `docked` holds; when it does not hold the weld still succeeds in the simulation and the absorbed hull jumps by `delta_abs` in the exterior layer only (reachable only in the residual window of E-17; the camera cut does not hide it, BDY-27, and the former fallback of dropping the `docked` term is deleted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
667	
668	**Example (DA-10):** `offset_a = (0, 0)`, `pos_a = (720, 672)`, `pos_b = (24, 288)`, `offset_b_old = (0, 0)`: `frame_shift_px = (0 + 720 - 24 - 0, 0 + 672 - 288 - 0) = (696, 384)` (29 x 24 and 16 x 24). With `world(home) = (1000, 500)` and `world(B) = (1696, 884)`, equal velocity: `world(b) - world(a) = (696, 384)`, docked, `delta_abs = (0, 0)`. An actor on B at `pos_curr = (100, 300)` has `abs = (1696, 884) + (100, 300) = (1796, 1184)` before; BM3 gives `pos_curr = (796, 684)` in the host frame, `abs = (1000, 500) + (796, 684) = (1796, 1184)`: equal. Not docked (`world(B) = (1720, 884)`): the difference is `(720, 384)`, `delta_abs = (696, 384) - (720, 384) = (-24, 0)`, the case the offer gate keeps away from the player. (Layout's own `LY D.6` example, `(576, 96)`, is a different socket placement and is not the MVP pair.) A weld followed by a cut of the same seam returns `pos_curr -= frame_shift_px` and zeroes the sub-pixel part, so it is **not** an identity on `pos_curr`; tests assert `abs` and section-local position.
669	
670	### D.6 Cut mode
671	
672	The cut_mode formula is defined as:
673	
674	`cut_mode(seam) = SEALED if ( for all o in openings(seam): area(o) == 0 ) AND ( for all e in fluid_sub_edges(seam): valve(e) == CLOSED ) AND ( for all c in cable_sub_edges(seam): breaker(c) == OPEN ), else RAGGED`
675	
676	Derived: the three clauses are exactly the as-welded state `weld_join` leaves (`LSG D.14`: opening `area` 0, valves CLOSED, breaker OPEN). The test reads **positions only**, never `hp`, `state` or `served_pm`. It is evaluated once, in the completion `apply` (step A1), and the single result is passed identically to M3 and LM3. No payload, prompt or cue carries or names a mode.
677	
678	**Variables:**
679	
680	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
681	|---|---|---|---|---|
682	| `area(o)` | int | 0..`area_max` | Graph via `seam_view` (ASK G3) | Opening area (the hatch) |
683	| `valve(e)` | enum | `OPEN`, `CLOSED` | Graph via `seam_view` | PIPE and DUCT sub-edge valve position |
684	| `breaker(c)` | enum | `OPEN`, `CLOSED` | Graph via `seam_view` | CABLE sub-edge breaker position |
685	| `cut_mode` | enum | `SEALED`, `RAGGED` | calculated | The `boundary_mode` for M3 and LM3 |
686	
687	**Output Range:** two values, deterministic. SEALED: nothing leaks, the socket becomes `CAPPED`, tombstones with a cap plate. RAGGED: per former opening a virtual hole `A_CUT` 24 on each side as a hull stub of `hp` 2500 (severity 4 BREACH, EXOGENOUS, exempt from the fairness gate, LS-16), each fluid port an `open_end` leaking at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` 500 until `cap_port`; a 20-tile room reaches the DECOMP band in 382 steps (38 s) and VACUUM in 960 steps (96 s) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the socket becomes `CUT_OPEN`. All cited from the Graph.
688	
689	**Example (MVP seam: one hatch OPENING, one O2 DUCT sub-edge, one POWER CABLE sub-edge):**
690	
691	| hatch `area` | O2 valve | breaker | `cut_mode` | what the player saw beforehand |
692	|---|---|---|---|---|
693	| 0 | CLOSED | OPEN | SEALED | a quiet seam: no creak, no frost, no valve hiss, no draught *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the bead's own weep hiss may still be present during wear-in and says nothing about the mode, MSA-23 item 1)* |
694	| 64 (open) | CLOSED | OPEN | RAGGED | the leaf standing open with a draught across the threshold |
695	| 0 | OPEN | OPEN | RAGGED | a hiss at the open valve's lane |
696	| 0 | CLOSED | CLOSED | RAGGED | the junction's own powered state |
697	| 64 | OPEN | CLOSED | RAGGED | all three |
698	| 0 | OPEN | CLOSED | RAGGED | the open valve's hiss and the junction's powered state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
699	| 64 | CLOSED | CLOSED | RAGGED | the open leaf with a draught and the junction's powered state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
700	| 64 | OPEN | OPEN | RAGGED | the open leaf with a draught and the open valve's hiss *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
701	
702	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the matrix is now all eight combinations of hatch, valve and breaker. Two quantifier cases follow from the formula and are tested with it: a hatch at `area` 1 (partly open) is RAGGED because only `area` 0 satisfies the first clause, and a seam with two openings is SEALED only if **both** are 0, so one at `area` 0 and one at `area` 1 is RAGGED.)*
703	
704	A hatch closed but a hallucinated "closed" valve that is truly open: RAGGED; the hiss is the consequence-channel witness the player could have heard (MSA-23). A hatch opened during a cancelled-and-resumed cut makes the resumed cut RAGGED because the mode is re-derived at completion.
705	
706	### D.7 Channel timing and exposure
707	
708	The channel_timing formula is defined as:
709	
710	`T_done = Tb + D - resume_offset` ; `T_apply = T_done + 1` ; `blocks = D / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` ; `exposure_s = ( D - resume_offset ) / TICK_RATE` ; `tool_pushes = D - resume_offset` ; constraint `D mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == 0`
711	
712	Derived: the clock, the abort set, the ledger and the noise are Interaction's (IA-14, IA-16, IA-33); Assembly supplies only `D` and consumes `T_done`. Accrual is at `e = T - Tb` = 1 to `D - resume_offset`, so the DONE handoff is the P3 of tick `T_done` and the completion applies in the P2 of `T_apply` (MSA-3). `resume_offset = blocks_done x B` while the ledger entry is valid (`T - abort_tick <= PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`), else 0 (`IA D.6`, cited). A cancel wastes at most `B - 1` accrued ticks (the partial block is not credited), so cancel-to-peek is never free. **Minimum resumed channel** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `D - resume_offset` can be as small as `B` = 6 ticks (one Graph block left), which is why the BUSY gate of D.11, not a channel-length floor, guards the handoff.
713	
714	**Variables:**
715	
716	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
717	|---|---|---|---|---|
718	| `Tb` | int64 tick | >= 0 | the P2 tick of `begin_*` | Begin tick (held as two 32-bit integers or a string at the serialisation boundary, SL-2) |
719	| `D` | int ticks | 240-480, multiple of 6 | `WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS` 360 / `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | Declared duration |
720	| `resume_offset` | int ticks | 0..`D - B` | Interaction ledger (cited) | Credited ticks from an earlier aborted channel |
721	| `B` = `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int | 6 | Graph (cited) | Block length |
722	| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 | Kernel (cited) | Ticks per second |
723	| `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` | int | 600 | Interaction (cited) | Ledger lifetime |
724	
725	**Output Range:** `blocks` 40 to 80; exposure 4.0 s (cut) to 8.0 s (weld at 480) fresh; `T_apply - Tb = D + 1` for a fresh channel. The floor 240 keeps both channels in the LONG bar class (`BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` 240); the ceiling 480 is set by analogy with IA I-9, not a lock on Assembly.
726	
727	**Example:** a fresh weld begins in P2 of `Tb` = 437039: `D` 360, `blocks` 60, accrual on ticks 437040..437399, `T_done` 437399, `T_apply` 437400; 360 TOOL pushes, exposure 6.0 s, **no** LOUD at the completion. A fresh seam cut begins at `Tb` = 439759: `D` 240, `T_done` 439999, `T_apply` 440000, 240 TOOL pushes and one LOUD at DONE (pushed by Interaction), exposure 4.0 s. A weld cancelled by movement at `e` = 100 credits block 16 (`resume_offset` 96); a re-begin within 600 ticks has remaining `360 - 96` = 264 ticks (4.4 s), so the total accrued TOOL ticks are 99 + 264 = 363, three more than the fresh 360 (the wasted partial block).
728	
729	### D.8 Body-count bound
730	
731	The bodies_after_worst_sequence formula is defined as:
732	
733	`N(t) = N0 - W(t) + C(t)` with `C(t) <= W(t)`, therefore `N(t) <= N0` for every reachable sequence; `bodies_after_worst_sequence = N0`; lint `N0 <= min( MAX_BODIES , BODIES_LIVE_MAX )`
734	
735	Derived: a weld merges two bodies into one (the absorbed body is `DISSOLVED`), a cut splits one into two, and every cut needs a prior `ACTIVE` weld, so cuts never outnumber welds. Sockets are terminal (LY-13), so `W <= P`, the number of authored socket pairs. Assembly adds no capacity rule; `can_detach`'s `CAPACITY` reason and a `MAX_SECTIONS_PER_BODY` value are deferred to Vertical Slice (Layout Open Question 8).
736	
737	**Variables:**
738	
739	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
740	|---|---|---|---|---|
741	| `N0` | int | 1..`MAX_BODIES` | built at load (Web Map `init_world`, Layout) | Live bodies before any Assembly command |
742	| `W(t)`, `C(t)` | int | 0..`P`; 0..`W(t)` | count of Layout `welds[]` rows ever welded / ever cut | Welds and cuts applied by tick `t` |
743	| `P` | int | MVP 1 | authored socket pairs | Possible welds |
744	| `MAX_BODIES` | int | 8 | Layout (cited, locked) | Hard cap |
745	| `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` | int | 4 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | 2D Lighting (cited) | Cross-body lighting cap |
746	
747	**Output Range:** MVP `N(t)` is 4 before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut. **Zero margin:** the worst case equals `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` exactly. Any body added outside Assembly (a second pod, a loose piece Web Map keeps alive) or any Vertical Slice socket-economy change exceeds it, which degrades cross-body lighting (stand-ins) without breaking the sim (MSA-41, ASK LT1). **Example:** home + A + B + pod = 4; weld (B dissolves into home): `4 - 1 + 0` = 3; cut: `4 - 1 + 1` = 4; a second weld attempt returns `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, so `N` stays 4 and `4 <= min(8, 4)` holds with margin 0.

content.content:
**Owner rule for `SYSTEM`-submitting hooks** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The pending queue is kernel data, not a block, so it is not in a snapshot, and a `SYSTEM` rejection is invisible to hooks (results go to the log only). A hook that submits `SYSTEM` commands (Assembly's `weld` / `seam_cut` completions, Transit's `pod_*`, Horror) must therefore be **restart-safe and rejection-tolerant**: its decision to submit is a function of persisted state, so after a restore (pending queue empty, `Dropped(RELOAD)`) it simply decides again; the completions are idempotent; timeouts are expressed in state (`submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1`), never as 'wait for the result'. A divisor-1 hook must guard re-submission with `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)` (or a `dedupe_key` on `submit_system`), because while the queue is backlogged it would otherwise queue a duplicate every tick. G4 (CR-13) holds only for owners that obey this rule.

content.content:
## Summary

Modular Ship Assembly is the system behind the game's first promise, "a body they assembled from the corpses of other ships": it owns the three physical acts that change the ship's shape (weld a derelict section onto the home-ship, cut a welded section away along its seam, and seat a carried module into a pre-shaped bay) and the single number of workmanship behind every weld. It does so as a thin orchestrator of one atomic, no-rollback command per act across the Life-Support Graph, the ship layout and the ship body, with no menu and no meter: the player sees a bead, a scar, a seated module and a seam that weeps, and learns whether a cut will be clean from the world before they press the button. Read this GDD if you touch welding, cutting, module install, the channel-then-apply handoff, the seam's life after the weld, or the riskiest MVP build item (the first spike).

> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed, hard); Life-Support Graph (designed, hard); Item & Module Database (designed, hard); Interaction System (designed, hard); Ship Section & Layout Data Model (designed, hard); Ship Body & Interior Physics (designed, hard); Save/Load & Versioned Format (designed, soft); Player Controller & Input and Suit & Equipment (designed, soft); Web Map & Transit (designed, hard for the offer); Boarding & Salvage (designed, hard: Boarding depends on Assembly); Adaptive Audio & Tells (designed, soft); HUD & Suit Layer (designed, soft); Sanity & Hallucination Rules (designed, soft); Perception Filter (designed, soft); Debug Overlay (designed, soft); Horror Entities (designed, soft)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: every "undesigned" and "draft in flight" marker refreshed; all of these files carry Status: Designed)*

## Overview

**Modular Ship Assembly is the system that changes the shape of the ship: it owns the three player commands that weld a derelict section onto the home-ship, cut a welded section away along its seam, and seat a carried module into a hardpoint, plus the one number of workmanship (`q`) that colours every weld.** At the data layer it is a thin orchestrator over four other owners' state. A weld or a cut is one atomic cross-block command whose `apply` calls published mutators on the Life-Support Graph (M2 `weld_join` / M3 `cut_detach`), Ship Section & Layout (LM2 `attach_section` / LM3 `detach_section`) and Ship Body (BM3 `rebase_on_attach` / BM4 `rebase_on_detach`) in one `WriteScope`, in that order, with no rollback (kernel CR-9); an install is a smaller atomic command that calls the Graph's M5 `install_module`, the Suit's `release_carried`, the Controller's `clear_carry_ref` (published, PC-1 b; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) and Interaction's `sync_section`. Assembly owns no geometry (Layout), no seam edges or atmosphere (Graph), no pose or actors (Body), no item vocabulary (Item DB), no channel clock or noise (Interaction). What it does own is small and exact: the five command types, the weld quality `q` (`WELD_Q_DEFAULT`), the channel durations (`WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS`, `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS`), the offer predicates (`weld_offer`, `seam_cut_offer`), the derivation of the cut mode from true state, the order of calls inside each apply, one outcome block (`assembly.state`) with one hook (`assembly.step`), and its own reason codes (`MSA.*`). Its hard job follows from the kernel's failure model: because there is no rollback, every precondition of every call inside an `apply` must be provable by a pure read in `validate`, so most of this document is the list of those

The player meets Assembly as a physical act, never as a menu. Docked beside a dead ship's airlock, lit and holding a welder, they hold `E · Weld` for six seconds, standing still while the web may be listening; a four-pixel Hull Grey bead appears across the frame and two hulls become one body. Nothing else happens: a weld moves nothing, the hatch is still shut, the valves still closed, the breaker still open, and the seam weeps faintly through the area the Graph gives it. Making the graft live is the player's own later work (open the hatch, open the valve, close the breaker, each a lit Interaction verb with its own physical answer). With the cutter they can later cut the section away along that same seam, clean if they prepared it and ragged (a breach on both sides) if they did not; the cut leaves a cap plate or a ragged scar that never goes away. Carrying a salvaged scrubber or heater home, one press seats it into a pre-shaped hardpoint with a clunk, and the machine either turns or does not. The bead, the cap plate, the scar and the seated module are the player's visible history on the ship; none of them is ever a number.

Without this system the game's first promise has no verb: "a body they assembled from the corpses of other ships" is a sentence, derelict sections could only be stripped and abandoned, a salvaged module would have nowhere to go, and Pillar 5 (salvage integrates into the body that survives; scarcity pushes inward; loss costs ship and body, never knowledge) would have no ship-shaped record to point at. It is also the kernel's stress test (kernel Interactions row 5: "Atomicity (G2, CR-9), one notification batch, validate-then-apply") and the riskiest MVP build item (index risk PR-SCOPE), so it is the first spike.

**Index reconciliation.** The index carries this system under three numbers that all name the same row: bullet 13 of the Systems Enumeration, entry 9 of the Feature layer in the Dependency Map, and row 16 of the Recommended Design Order. The index wording ("Weld and cut sections as atomic one-tick commands across graph join and layout change: join validation is a pure Graph query; seams set edge properties; cap plates; detach into a new body. Also owns module install/uninstall ... as a graph mutation distinct from section welding") is honoured with five readings, each routed where it differs. (1) *Atomic one-tick*: the **completion** command is atomic in one tick; the player-facing act is a four-to-six-second channel followed by that tick (MSA-3). findings.section: Edge Cases E-31; AC-MSA-130; MSA-33 (Save & Quit); consequence of delegated ruling R15 with D54
findings.finding: A Save & Quit inside the open RAGGED window is written RISKY with risky_cause ASSEMBLY_BREACH, and Assembly accepts it. Save/Load SL-8's RISKY-window route excludes a QUIT generation unless its risky_cause contains VITALS, and R15 exempts such a QUIT from the fairness step-back. A QUIT taken mid-vent with a non-CRITICAL suit is therefore never demoted. Continue restores it as the newest non-demoted generation. If the avatar then dies (for example a quit at the far wall with little time left), the death restart restores the same QUIT again. MVP death is 'restart from the last autosave', so that is a possible repeating loop with no exit, which is the unfair reload D54 rules out. AC-MSA-130 enumerates the QUIT generation but only asserts winnability for the first clean generation after t_vac.
findings.fix: Either extend AC-MSA-130 to restore the mid-window QUIT generation and assert the winnable condition, or have Save/Load treat ASSEMBLY_BREACH like VITALS for the QUIT exemption (a QUIT whose risky_cause includes ASSEMBLY_BREACH is not exempt from demotion). State the choice in E-31 under a delegated ruling (G2 lean: the narrower change to the exemption).

findings.section: Formulas D.9 (event_due, last_shape_change_T row); AC-MSA-54; MSA-33; Open Question 45; registry last_shape_change_T

findings.section: Formulas D.1; MSA-13; Tuning Knobs T17; AC-MSA-18; registry weld_quality
findings.finding: Carried-over from the 3rd review (item 3): Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP/10)) still ignores BREACH_HP. Assembly's registry entry records the Graph's request as 'declined here until the owner conforms'. BREACH_HP is tunable 1000-6000 (default 4000), LEAK_HP 2000-6000. At defaults both are 4000, so nothing is wrong. Any BREACH_HP above LEAK_HP (for example 5000) lets a legal q of 400 to 499 start the seam below BREACH_HP, with no tell. findings.section: MSA-33; Formulas D.9 ragged_breach_open row; Dependencies T13/T15 (L1)
findings.finding: Implementability gap in the new predicate. venting(s) and ports_open(s) filter on keep_sections(s), which the GDD sources from Layout's detach_preview. detach_preview is a pre-cut prediction ('computed without mutation', body pre-cut frame, intended for an ACTIVE seam). ragged_breach_open() evaluates seams already in state CUT_RAGGED, long after the cut. Layout's welds[] row is {seam_id, section_a, socket_a, section_b, socket_b, welded_at_T, state, cut_at_T} and records no keep side. assembly.state holds outcomes only (MSA-4). findings.fix: State the derivation: the keep side of a CUT seam is the section among {section_a, section_b} whose body_of() is the body that holds the original origin_section_id (or whichever section currently shares body_id with the pre-cut body). Alternatively ask Layout to record keep_sections on the welds[] row at LM3.

findings.section: Edge Cases E-31; AC-MSA-130; MSA-33 (Save & Quit); consequence of delegated ruling R15 with D54
findings.finding: A Save & Quit inside the open RAGGED window is written RISKY with risky_cause ASSEMBLY_BREACH, and Assembly accepts it. Save/Load SL-8's RISKY-window route excludes a QUIT generation unless its risky_cause contains VITALS, and R15 exempts such a QUIT from the fairness step-back. A QUIT taken mid-vent with a non-CRITICAL suit is therefore never demoted. Continue restores it as the newest non-demoted generation. If the avatar then dies (for example a quit at the far wall with little time left), the death restart restores the same QUIT again. MVP death is 'restart from the last autosave', so that is a possible repeating loop with no exit, which is the unfair reload D54 rules out. AC-MSA-130 enumerates the QUIT generation but only asserts winnability for the first clean generation after t_vac.
findings.fix: Either extend AC-MSA-130 to restore the mid-window QUIT generation and assert the winnable condition, or have Save/Load treat ASSEMBLY_BREACH like VITALS for the QUIT exemption (a QUIT whose risky_cause includes ASSEMBLY_BREACH is not exempt from demotion). State the choice in E-31 under a delegated ruling (G2 lean: the narrower change to the exemption).

Add it to D.9 and to the L1 ask as a pure read on persisted state, and add an AC that ragged_breach_open() gives the same answer before and after a snapshot/restore mid-vent. Alternatively ask Layout to record keep_sections on the welds[] row at LM3.

findings.section: Edge Cases E-31; AC-MSA-130; MSA-33 (Save & Quit); consequence of delegated ruling R15 with D54
findings.finding: A Save & Quit inside the open RAGGED window is written RISKY with risky_cause ASSEMBLY_BREACH, and Assembly accepts it. Save/Load SL-8's RISKY-window route excludes a QUIT generation unless its risky_cause contains VITALS, and R15 exempts such a QUIT from the fairness step-back. A QUIT taken mid-vent with a non-CRITICAL suit is therefore never demoted. Continue restores it as the newest non-demoted generation. If the avatar then dies (for example a quit at the far wall with little time left), the death restart restores the same QUIT again. MVP death is 'restart from the last autosave', so that is a possible repeating loop with no exit, which is the unfair reload D54 rules out. AC-MSA-130 enumerates the QUIT generation but only asserts winnability for the first clean generation after t_vac.
findings.fix: Either extend AC-MSA-130 to restore the mid-window QUIT generation and assert the winnable condition, or have Save/Load treat ASSEMBLY_BREACH like VITALS for the QUIT exemption (a QUIT whose risky_cause includes ASSEMBLY_BREACH is not exempt from demotion). State the choice in E-31 under a delegated ruling (G2 lean: the narrower change to the exemption).

findings.section: Player Fantasy; MSA-23b; Dependencies (In-World Instruments row, ASK IW1); Open Question 37; line citations 'L44 and L76'
findings.finding: Carried-over (3rd review, items 'IW1' and 'line numbers'). (1) The headline 'put my hand on the seam' fantasy still rests on ASK IW1. in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md has no Assembly text, and the dependency is explicitly one-way, which breaks the bidirectional-dependency rule. Under G6, a GAP (the owner lacks a surface the consumer's ruled behaviour needs) is fixed by the OWNER ADDING it, so 'unanswered' should not survive this pass. (2) The citations 'Player Fantasy L44 and L76' (MSA-23b, T13, T15 IW1, AC-MSA-145, OQ 37) point at blank lines (L44 and L76 are empty; the co-op beat is at L49), against the GDD's own no-line-number convention.
findings.fix: Add the QUIET seam inspect read to the Inspect View GDD (a short rule, one AC, an Assembly row) and mark IW1 answered. If that is out of scope for this pass, record it under R21 as a deferred gap with the permanent MSA-23 fallback. In both cases replace 'L44/L76' with the section anchors ('Anchor moments, the cut' and 'Under hallucination the fantasy deepens').

findings.section: Dependencies T13 (Life-Support Graph row, Save/Load row) and T15 (G10, S1, D2/D3); AC-MSA-76 'depends' tag
findings.finding: Stale status text after this pass. The T13 Graph row still says 'G1 to G3 answered; G4 to G10 open', and the G10 row is not marked ANSWERED, although the Graph now publishes cut_sides and compartment(cid).band_p (LS-15/LS-16/LS-19) and AC-MSA-76 itself says 'answered by Graph LS-16 / seam_view'. findings.section: MSA-33 (listed exposure formula)
findings.finding: The worst-case venting formula is typo'd: ceil(ln(10) x V_total x 1000 / (2 x 24 x 1000)) evaluates to 6 for V_total = 120, not 5757 steps. The extra GAS_SCALE factor cancels. 5757 steps (34,542 ticks) is correct only if the numerator keeps GAS_SCALE and the denominator is G_OPEN x A_CUT.
findings.fix: Write steps = ceil(ln(10) x V_total x GAS_SCALE / (G_OPEN x A_CUT x n_holes)) = ceil(2.302585 x 120 x 1000 / 48) = 5757.

findings.section: AC-MSA-130 (ii)
findings.finding: The winnability check for saved avatar positions (A)/(B)/(C) is satisfied by 'the fixture pins' the saved suit reserve, so it proves the scripted route works but not that every permitted generation is winnable. The guarantee actually comes from Suit's CRITICAL gate (vitals_block) and the reserve/traverse coupling (reserve 90 s at RESERVE_S; V_WALK 2 px/tick makes a 20-tile crossing about 8 s). The AC does not derive that bound.
findings.fix: Add one numeric assertion: for every position in the vented room, ceil(path_px / V_WALK) / TICK_RATE < reserve_s at the CRITICAL threshold, using Suit's registered constants.

findings.section: Formulas D.9 note (b) / MSA-33 'ends by construction'
findings.finding: The text says venting 'ends by construction' with a residual of at most ceil(1/k) mGU and does not mention gas supply into the room. At the Graph defaults (R_VENT 600, R_MAKEUP 1800 per step) the supplied equilibrium (about 12 to 38 dkPa) stays below the VACUUM threshold, so the claim holds. It would stop holding if a vent budget were raised about 3x or 8 vents fed one room, and venting has no ceiling.
findings.fix: State the precondition (steady-state supply pressure P* = supply/(k x V x GAS_SCALE) < 100 dkPa at the registry defaults) and add a content or boot lint, or give venting a very long safety ceiling that routes to the RISKY interval path.

data.summary: Verdict: no BLOCKING findings, so this pass can close; I would call it APPROVED WITH RECOMMENDATIONS. The one prior blocker, the D54 RAGGED autosave withhold, is genuinely fixed and consistent in this GDD, the Graph (LS-15/LS-16), Save/Load (SL-4, F-1, SL-5 row (d), AC-SL-144) and the registry. The new predicate is `venting OR ports_open`. Capping ports no longer releases the withhold, the hole clause ends on the Graph band VACUUM, no repair verb was invented, and the arithmetic holds when recomputed by hand. Formulas D.1 to D.18, the D.5 offset worked example, the D.7 timing example and the D.11 TTL example, the D.14 subject budget (143/175) and the D.15 budget sum recompute correctly. The cross-GDD edits of this pass (BM4 `rects[]`, Graph tick stagger, S_int/S_total 143/175, R12 machines) agree with Body, Layout, Graph and Interaction. The R20 'confirmed' markers are applied and no open 'USER DECISION' or X14 wording remains, apart from the odd '300 warm-up ticks' remnant. The structure check passes (all 8 sections) and every dependency GDD exists. Remaining issues are RECOMMENDED: (1) AC-MSA-54/D.9 still assert a settle term and kind-free withhold that Save/Load, the owner, does not adopt, and the registry carries two event_due expressions; (2) Q_MIN still ignores BREACH_HP, which the Graph already requested; (3) keep_sections has no stated source for an already-cut seam or after a restore; (4) a Save & Quit mid-vent (RISKY, ASSEMBLY_BREACH) is not demoted under R15/SL-8 and can loop on death; (5) the IW1 ask is still one-way and the 'L44/L76' citations point at blank lines; (6) stale ASK status rows (G10, S1, D2, cap_duct_junction). Several are 3rd-review RECOMMENDED items that have still not landed (G3), so the next fix pass should do them first and then grep the old wording.
